title: 3AM minutiae pocketbook (on-call sketch)
content:
Purpose: a compact, slightly messy pocketbook for the 3AM bridge handover. Not polished — copy what you need.

Context summary:
- Night: steady traffic but a spike at ~02:10 UTC from a customer load test (unannounced) caused model-serving GPU saturation on pool 'hosted-v2'.
- Visible effects: increased request queuing, a few 504s for low-priority routes, token-generation latency spiked from 110ms -> 420ms p50/p90.
- Temporary mitigation applied: scaled dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-burst-1) up by +2 nodes and enabled prefix-KV cache bypass for the noisy route. Latency recovered by ~02:27 UTC.

Immediate items for incoming shift:
- Verify dedicated-burst-1 autoscaler stayed up and healthy (k8s hpa, nodewatch).
  - Command: kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=dedicated-burst-1 -o wide
  - Check node GPU memory: ssh to gce-node-34 -> nvidia-smi (watch for processes holding >30GB)
- Confirm cache bypass toggle reverted? We left bypass ON for noisy-route to prevent cache thrash. Decide if it should remain overnight.
- Review SLO alerts that fired: SLO-API-Gen-latency (pager), Route-504-threshold (ops), Token-Quota-warning (monitor).

Recent incident notes (rough chronology):
- 02:08 UTC: big customer (acct: ACCT-774) hit endpoint /v1/chat/generate in burst.
- 02:10 UTC: queue depth increase, p95 token latency > 350ms, frontline alerts triggered.
- 02:14 UTC: attempted auto-scale for hosted-v2 failed due to node allocation quota in us-west1 (we hit project quota).
- 02:16 UTC: manual scale of dedicated-burst-1 initiated; enabled cache bypass for route noisy-route.
- 02:27 UTC: latencies returned to baseline; alerts started to resolve.
- 02:35 UTC: follow-up: created JIRA-INC-4718 to track quota and guardrails.

What I changed while on call (so you can revert if needed):
- /infra/terraform: increased reserved nodes for dedicated-burst-1 (applied) — PR link in linked_artifacts.
- Ops flag: toggled route.noisy-route.cache.bypass = true in feature flags console (remember this is sticky until toggled back).
- Added temporary alert rule to detect quota-exhaustion on nodepool (alert name TEMP-QuotaNodepool).

Quick checks (5 minutes):
- Grafana: open dashboard `infra/pool-health` and look at GPU mem utilization, queue depth (time window 02:00-03:00).
- Datadog: search for trace errors with tag route:noisy-route and response.status:504.
- Billing/quotas: GCP console -> compute quotas -> filter by us-west1 GPUs.
- Slack: #ops-night for any customer comms; threads: pinned message from 02:40 has the incident timeline.

Escalation contacts (if node pool quota blocks scaling or we see persistent 504s):
- On-call SRE mgr: Marcus Li (pager: +1-415-555-0132, slack: @marcus)
- Infra Eng (quota + GCP): Priya Nair (slack: @priya, email: priya@redwood.com)
- Customer-success for ACCT-774: Sofia Gomez (slack: @sofia) — she is aware and starting a customer-notice draft.

Temp mitigations (if problem reappears):
- Immediate: route-level rate limit for ACCT-774 using API-GW per-user cap (slowly lower to 50rps).
- Fallback: route mapping -> reroute noisy-route to a cheaper quantized model (model: llama-q4b) via smart routing rules.
- If GPU quota: shift low-priority work to CPU-only pools for a short window (useful for batch & embeddings).

Open items / TODO (post-shift):
- Follow-up: add a quota safety check to scale logic to avoid failed scaling attempts (owner: infra; ticket JIRA-INC-4718).
- Postmortem: short RCA draft, include decision to leave cache bypass on and scaling failure due to quota. Target owner: me (Asha) + Marcus.
- Add a canary load-profile to catch customer-induced spikes in staging.

Notes to self (messy):
- Cache-bypass left ON intentionally — but can increase token costs. If no more spikes for 24h, revert and monitor.
- If you see sustained GPU mem > 90% on >2 nodes: consider draining non-critical pods (label: preemptible=true) before scaling down.
- The temporary alert TEMP-QuotaNodepool should be deleted after infra ticket resolved; I left it firing to ensure we see quota regressions.

Handoff checklist to copy/paste to incoming: (quick)
- [ ] Confirm dedicated-burst-1 pods healthy
- [ ] Check feature flag route.noisy-route.cache.bypass status and decide revert or keep
- [ ] Validate no new 504 alerts in past 30m
- [ ] Ping @sofia in CS: update customer comms status
- [ ] Start RCA draft if incident meets threshold

Open questions (for follow-up meeting):
- Should we implement per-customer admission control on the API side (hard caps + circuit breaker) to protect shared pools?
- Do we want automatic fallback to quantized model variants for noisy routes, or leave this manual?

If you need context mid-shift: DM me (slack: @ashap) or call +1-415-555-0177. If I don't respond immediately, escalate to Marcus.

End of quick notes. Feel free to trim and paste into the formal runbook if useful.

-- Asha
